name: Buena Vista Float
section: Arkansas River, Buena Vista to Ruby Mountain
klassNote: Flat water with a few riffles. You paddle when you feel like it.
dogNote: Dogs ride free on this one. Bring a harness.
blurb: Six miles of gentle water under the Collegiate Peaks. For small kids, grandparents, and anyone who would rather look at the mountains than at the next rapid.

name: Browns Canyon
section: Arkansas River, Hecla Junction to Ruby Mountain
klassNote: Continuous read-and-run rapids with a pool between each one.
dogNote: Dogs welcome at low water. Ask when you book.
blurb: The trip this river is known for. Ten miles of granite walls, named rapids and room to breathe between them. Most people's first real whitewater.

name: The Numbers
section: Arkansas River, Granite to Buena Vista
klassNote: Steep, technical and continuous. You paddle as a team or you swim.
blurb: Twelve miles named for the highway mileposts that count them off. The closest thing to a roller coaster that a river will give you without a motor.

name: Pine Creek
section: Arkansas River, Granite to Numbers put-in
klassNote: Big drops, tight lines, no room to drift. Best when the river drops.
blurb: Five miles, four big drops, and a canyon so narrow the sun only reaches it at noon. Runs best late in the season, when the rest of the river is falling.

name: Royal Gorge
section: Arkansas River, Parkdale to Canon City
klassNote: Class V at high water. You will be asked about your experience.
blurb: Ten miles under the highest suspension bridge in North America, through a canyon a thousand feet deep. The biggest water we guide, and the only trip we turn people away from.

name: Granite Camp
section: Arkansas River, Granite to Buena Vista, with a night on the bank
klassNote: Two days of class III, with time to swim and fish between rapids.
dogNote: Dogs welcome. They sleep in the camp, not the raft.
blurb: Two days, eighteen miles, one night camped on the bank above Clear Creek. We haul the food, the tents and the fire pan; you haul nothing.
